summary: Operational utility scripts: structured telemetry (log-event.sh/log-phase.sh), layered TOML config + model routing (config.py/config.sh), the lockless active-plan registry with F1-F5 cross-session lease/wait/claim primitives (active-plan-registry.py), the git-safety PreToolUse hook (block-dangerous-git.sh), memory/dismissal maintenance scripts, remote sandbox sync, and persona-rotation analysis.

entry_points.summary: PreToolUse hook blocking dangerous git ops; reads hook JSON from stdin; two verb classes: rewrite (upstream-reachability check) and working-tree-destructive (blanket-block); normalizes commands (strips global options, chains); Z_HARNESS_GIT_GUARDRAILS_OVERRIDE=1 override; fail-closed on git errors.

Bash test harness for block-dangerous-git.sh; 7 TEST groups (T005-A through T005-G); covers destructive-block, pass-through, upstream-reachable block, local-only allow, fail-closed, override+audit-log, and global-option/chaining evasion regression.

Appends structured JSON event to run events.jsonl and repo-wide metrics.jsonl; resolves base via z_harness_base() 5-tier fallback from plan-path.sh; flock-safe; Z_HARNESS_BASE_DIR external-base redirect; mid-flight legacy run detection (skipped when Z_HARNESS_BASE_DIR set); resolve-run-dir subcommand for read-only path lookup; when HERMES_MARKER_FILE is set, also fires emit-hermes-marker.sh (status, or heartbeat for context_pressure kind) as a best-effort trailing step.

Sugar over log-event.sh; five modes: start/end (token-based, in-process), begin/finish (file-persisted to $TMPDIR, survives cross-Bash-tool-call boundaries), wrap (end-to-end command timing); python3 ms-timestamp fallback for macOS; anomaly detection via check_wall_ms.
Anomaly guard: emits telemetry_anomaly and suppresses *_end event when wall_ms > 604_800_000ms or wall_ms < 0.
Scans docs/llm/*.json, collects memories[], sorts by slug asc/date desc, writes MEMORIES-FLAT.md atomically via os.replace.
Emits JSON blob with plugin git SHA, dirty flag, branch, optional tag; resolves plugin root via four env vars.

Gate script for memory-review agent, called by /z-execute, /z-review-all, and /z-debug; <RUN> <parent_command>; 4-state terminal taxonomy; stdout contract on ready: STATUS: ready, diff path, SPEC path (or empty), TAGS path, optional DEBUG.md path; final line AXIOM_READY <diff-path> when axioms.auto_extract_post_run != 'false'.
CLI: extracts dismissed finding signatures from consecutive archive run pairs; --global and --filename flags; outputs {signatures,n_runs_scanned}.
Pairwise algorithm: R_i snapshot vs R_{i+1}.previous-* user-edited copy to find dismissed findings.

Rsync local tree to two-level remote layout under sandbox/: <slug>/base/ (seeded once, atomic mkdir lock) + <slug>/<task-id>/ overlay via --link-dest; optional --sandbox-key <slug>/<subpath> overrides the overlay path (used by coalesced per-BFS-level REMOTE_VERIFY dispatch, e.g. <slug>/level-<N>) while the shared warm base stays keyed by SLUG alone; REMOTE_HOME resolved via SSH printf; SLUG/TASK_ID/SANDBOX_KEY validated against path-traversal; sandbox/ sub-dir prevents stray rsync from polluting container root; Z_HARNESS_WORKTREE_ROOT overrides the default git-rev-parse-show-toplevel source root.
Acquires remote lock via mkdir, seeds shared base via rsync, writes .base-ready marker with HEAD SHA, releases lock; losers poll up to 600s.

Layered TOML config loader; subcommands: get, get-batch, export-env, ensure-defaults, explain, should-notify, list-question-ids, resolve-question, resolve-halt-category, check-no-ask, set, migrate, inspect-all; QUESTION_IDS registry + RESULT_MAP + [followup] section + model_classes/model_routing dynamic-key sections; startup guards at module load.

New DEFAULTS sections: model_classes.{cheap,standard,deep}.{model,thinking,reasoning} (local model-class routing) and model_routing.native_agents.default / model_routing.implementer.{low,medium,high,retry} (implementer tier→model labels, e.g. sonnet/opus/gpt-5.5).
Module-load guard: asserts QUESTION_IDS keys exist in VALIDATORS, have skill_default, have a halt_category in HALT_CATEGORY_ENUM (guard 2b), and RESULT_MAP choices are valid; exits 2 on violation.
Prints sorted JSON array of registered question IDs from QUESTION_IDS registry.
Resolves multiple config keys in a single process; prints JSON object {key:val,...}; unknown keys null+warn to stderr; meta keys excluded; always exits 0 (best-effort).
Prints halt_category tag for given question_id; fail-safe default 'ask' for unknown/untagged qids; bare string output (not JSON); exits 2 with no arguments.

Returns JSON resolver envelope {result,default,source,rule_id,strength,reason,sources}; result in {ask,skip,prefill,halt,defer-to-sink}; consults 4-layer config then routing-preference memories; honors Z_HARNESS_ASK_ALL, Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK, Z_HARNESS_EXPLAIN_RESOLUTION; exits 5 when both conflicting env vars set.
Returns JSON {result:halt|proceed, question_id, rule_id}; fail-closed gate for overnight mode; unregistered qids always halt with unknown_ask_blocked event.

Atomic read-modify-write of config key in global or project TOML; validates key+value before writing; model_classes/model_routing keys route through dynamic-key validators (_dynamic_model_config_validator); exit 2 on validation, 4 on I/O.
Thin shell wrapper: exec python3 scripts/config.py "$@".

Lockless per-run active-plan registry; 11 subcommands (session-id, register, heartbeat, update-scope, list, deregister, overlaps, reap, claim, release, wait-for); all writes atomic via tmpfile+os.replace; no global lock; resolves active_plans_dir via plan-path.sh; Z_HARNESS_REGISTRY_ENABLED=0 silences all coordination writes. claim/release/wait-for implement the cross-session lease/wait subsystem (F1-F5): wait/lease gates only the waiter's own run, takes no lock, never writes a peer's record except the reaper's stale-marking exception, and every wait has a finite budget + loud timeout.
Prints stable session-id token: echoes Z_HARNESS_SESSION_ID if set; otherwise derives <ppid>-<start_epoch> (Linux /proc) or <ppid>-<epoch> (macOS pure-Python fallback, no subprocess). Always exits 0.

Writes schema-v1 record atomically; validates run-id as safe basename (^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, no leading dash, no '..'); accepts optional --watchdog-pid (advisory field); LOUD failure exit 3; emits plan_registered.
Updates last_heartbeat/phase/current_task/status (+ optional --watchdog-pid); NON-FATAL (always 0); absent record emits registry_error(reason:missing_record) — does NOT fabricate zombie records.
Merges scope array [{path,confidence,reason}] into record; NON-FATAL; self-logs registry_error on internal error.

Atomically unlinks the run's record (FileNotFoundError on unlink is benign); reads the .watchdog.pid file for the run's slug plan dir and SIGTERM->grace->SIGKILLs the watchdog sweep (best-effort, NON-FATAL); emits plan_deregistered.

Best-effort path-lease claim; stages requested paths, re-reads all peer records (F2 check-after-claim), resolves contention by run_id lexicographic tiebreak (only senior peers — lower run_id — can force a concession), persists the won set into held_paths. Prints {claimed:[...], conceded:[{path,holder_run_id}]}; always exits 0.
Best-effort release of held_paths (named subset via --paths or --all); refreshes last_heartbeat; emits lease_released{run_id,paths}; NON-FATAL, always exits 0.

Parks the caller's run behind one or more senior peers (--on) until their records clear (gone/complete/aborted/stale) or the budget expires; auto mode (runtime.auto_wait) uses runtime.auto_wait_budget_secs, explicit mode uses Z_HARNESS_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS; polls at Z_HARNESS_WAIT_POLL_SECS; waiting_on is cleared on every exit path via try/finally (EH-005). Exit 0=cleared/nothing_to_wait_on, 2=usage error, 10=budget expired (LOUD), 130=SIGINT/SIGTERM.

Computes path intersection vs all live peer records; exit 0=no overlap, 10=advisory, 20=blocking (strict+explicit×explicit exact path match); same run-id or session-id skipped; stale peers included but non-blocking; emits scope_overlap_detected or active_plan_scan_complete.

Conservative reaper: (a) delete on dead-local-pid, (b) delete on age>2×stale_threshold, (c) mark status:stale on age>1×stale_threshold for remote/unknown hosts; FileNotFoundError on unlink is benign; this is the one allowed cross-record write (marking a peer stale); NON-FATAL overall; emits plan_reaped / plan_marked_stale.
Argument parser dispatch (11 subcommands); checks Z_HARNESS_REGISTRY_ENABLED=0 before executing mutating subcommands; overlaps returns 0 when disabled.

[rotation] Read-only analysis for persona-rotation experiment. Reads metrics.jsonl; joins persona_random_selected (draw) to persona_attempt_outcome (terminal) by attempt_id; groups by persona_id×role×complexity_tier; baseline resolution: no-persona first, boring-anchor second, None; reviewer rows from persona_bound; quarantines fallback_empty_pool; supports --json, --min-diff-size, --since, --include-unknown-run. Always read-only.
[rotation] String constant 'no-persona' — primary null baseline for delta computation within each (role, complexity_tier) stratum.
[rotation] String constant 'boring-anchor' — secondary bland control baseline (used when no-persona samples absent in the stratum).
[rotation] Tuple ('review_cycles','retries','blocker_count','wall_ms','diff_size') — metrics aggregated (mean) per group and delta'd vs baseline.
[rotation] Event kind string 'persona_attempt_outcome' — the terminal event joined against draw events.

End-to-end smoke tests for config.py; 25+ test classes with hermetic XDG_CONFIG_HOME temp dirs; covers defaults, env overrides, repo-local precedence, schema errors, ensure-defaults, export-env dedup, resolve-question, overnight overrides, check-no-ask, list-question-ids, 3-level nesting (roles.*), migrate, _KEY_RE, and the new model_classes/model_routing dynamic-key validation (release T: codex prod support + model routing).
Bash regression harness for log-phase.sh; 4 TEST groups, 21 assertions; hermetic via Z_HARNESS_PLANS_DIR+Z_HARNESS_SLUG temp dirs; covers overflow, normal path, negative wall_ms, 26h false-positive.

invariants: All scripts require python3 for JSON handling, timing fallbacks, and document generation.
All scripts resolve the repo root via git rev-parse or pwd fallback.
log-event.sh resolves artifact base via z_harness_base() from plan-path.sh (5-tier fallback); Z_HARNESS_BASE_DIR overrides all tiers.
log-event.sh and log-phase.sh honor Z_HARNESS_SLUG for slug-namespaced vs. legacy flat plan layout.
log-event.sh mid-flight legacy detection is skipped entirely when Z_HARNESS_BASE_DIR is set to preserve the model.patch invariant.

log-event.sh emits a best-effort Hermes marker via emit-hermes-marker.sh whenever HERMES_MARKER_FILE is set; emit-hermes-marker.sh itself is a strict no-op when that env var is unset, so the check in log-event.sh is a fast-path, not the sole gate.
log-phase.sh check_wall_ms emits telemetry_anomaly and suppresses *_end event when wall_ms > 604_800_000ms (overflow) or wall_ms < 0 (clock skew); exits 0 in both anomaly cases.
log-phase.sh begin mode writes T0 to $TMPDIR/z-harness-phase/<key>.start so wall_ms survives across separate Bash tool-call boundaries; finish is fail-open (no stamp = emit nothing, not wall_ms:0).
regenerate-memories-flat.py writes MEMORIES-FLAT.md atomically via os.replace on a PID+random-suffixed temp file.
run-memory-review.sh always exits 0; skip conditions are communicated via STATUS: line on stdout.
run-memory-review.sh accepts exactly two positional args: <RUN> <parent_command>.

run-memory-review.sh stdout line 1 is always STATUS: ready | STATUS: skipped <reason>; lines 2-4 are diff, SPEC (or empty), TAGS paths when ready; line 5 is DEBUG.md path when parent_command is debug; final line is AXIOM_READY <diff-path> when axioms.auto_extract_post_run != 'false'.

run-memory-review.sh emits exactly one memory_review_terminal event on all skip paths using a 4-state taxonomy: skipped_broken_context, not_applicable, ready (orchestrator-owned), dispatched (orchestrator-owned).
extract-dismissals.py outputs JSON {signatures, n_runs_scanned} to stdout; exit 0 even when no dismissals found.
extract-dismissals.py --global applies the pairwise algorithm within each slug independently, not across slugs.
The env var for the plan base dir is Z_HARNESS_PLAN_DIR (singular, not PLANS_DIR).

config.py _run_startup_guards() runs at module load and exits 2 on any QUESTION_IDS/VALIDATORS/RESULT_MAP/HALT_CATEGORY_ENUM inconsistency (four guards, including guard 2b: every question_id must have a halt_category in HALT_CATEGORY_ENUM).
config.py resolve-question returns a JSON envelope with result in {ask, skip, prefill, halt, defer-to-sink} (resolver result-domain); RESULT_MAP handles option-to-result translation.
config.py resolve-question stdout is reserved for the JSON envelope; all diagnostics route to stderr.
config.py resolve-question exits 5 when Z_HARNESS_ASK_ALL=1 and Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt are both set.
config.py check-no-ask is fail-closed: unregistered question_ids return halt when Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt.
config.py set performs atomic read-modify-write via temp-file rename; validates key format and value against VALIDATORS before writing; exit 2 on validation, 4 on I/O.
config.py export-env emits config_resolved event at most once per Z_HARNESS_RUN via O_EXCL stamp file in TMPDIR.
config.py get-batch always exits 0 (best-effort); unknown keys return null with stderr warning; meta keys are excluded.
config.py resolve-halt-category outputs a bare tag string (not JSON); fail-safe default 'ask' for unknown or untagged qids; exits 2 with no arguments.

config.py model_classes.<name>.{model,thinking,reasoning} and model_routing.{native_agents.default, implementer.low|medium|high|retry} are dynamic-key sections: keys are validated structurally (canonical lowercase/underscore segments, no nested tables) via _dynamic_model_config_validator rather than a fixed VALIDATORS entry per class name; a custom model class must define 'model' before optional thinking/reasoning metadata, else exit 2 (project) or WARNING+skip (global).
block-dangerous-git.sh exit contract: exit 0 = allow, exit 2 = block (with human-readable reason on stderr); never exits 1.
block-dangerous-git.sh never crashes on empty stdin, malformed JSON, or non-Bash tool calls — all fail safe (exit 0).
block-dangerous-git.sh classifies commands against canonical forms (global options stripped, chained segments split) so evasion via -C/-c/--git-dir/env-var-prefix is not possible.
block-dangerous-git.sh working-tree-destructive verbs (clean -f*, checkout ., restore ., branch -D) are blanket-blocked without any subprocess.
block-dangerous-git.sh rewrite verbs (reset --hard, commit --amend, push --force/--force-with-lease/-f, +-refspec push) are blocked iff git branch -r --contains HEAD returns non-empty output.
block-dangerous-git.sh is fail-closed: any git error during the upstream-reachability check results in a block (not an allow).
block-dangerous-git.sh +-refspec push detection requires the refspec to start with + AND have at least one character after the + (bare + is not a refspec).
Z_HARNESS_GIT_GUARDRAILS_OVERRIDE=1 writes exactly one audit entry per invocation to <base>/git-guardrails-audit.log; the override is one-shot, not a permanent disable.

active-plan-registry.py lockless invariant: lockless design is safe ONLY because overlap is advisory; no code may make overlap a hard gate without replacing lockless delete with compare-and-delete or a registry lock.

active-plan-registry.py wait/lease cross-cutting invariant (F1-F5): wait/lease gates only the waiter's OWN run; it takes no lock; it never writes a peer's record except the reaper's single-writer stale-marking exception; every wait has a finite budget + loud timeout; overlap is never a hard gate; the holder is never preempted.
active-plan-registry.py register exits 3 on failure (LOUD); all other subcommands exit 0 even on internal error (NON-FATAL), self-logging via registry_error events.
active-plan-registry.py heartbeat does NOT fabricate a record when target <run-id>.json is absent; emits registry_error(reason:missing_record) and returns 0.
active-plan-registry.py all writes use tmpfile+os.replace (atomic); no global lock is taken.
active-plan-registry.py overlaps blocking exit 20 requires both --strict (or Z_HARNESS_STRICT_OVERLAP=1) AND explicit×explicit exact path match with a non-stale peer.
active-plan-registry.py reap case (a): dead-local-pid → delete; case (b): age > 2×stale_threshold → delete; case (c): age > 1×stale_threshold AND remote/unknown host → mark status:stale (no delete).

active-plan-registry.py Z_HARNESS_REGISTRY_ENABLED=0: all mutating subcommands (register, heartbeat, update-scope, overlaps, reap, deregister, claim, release, wait-for) become silent no-ops; list and session-id are always permitted.
active-plan-registry.py run-id must match ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$, not start with '-', and contain no '..' or '/'.
active-plan-registry.py session-id: on macOS uses pure-Python <ppid>-<epoch> (no subprocess) to avoid CoreFoundation fork-safety crash.

active-plan-registry.py claim resolves contention by run_id lexicographic tiebreak: a claim only concedes to a SENIOR peer (lower run_id) holding the same path; junior peers never force a concession. A tiebreak loser's persisted held_paths must not contain the conceded path.

active-plan-registry.py wait-for clears the waiting_on field on every exit path via try/finally (EH-005), so no paused zombie record can leak even on SIGINT/SIGTERM (exit 130) or budget timeout (exit 10).

active-plan-registry.py deregister reads the run's slug's .watchdog.pid file and SIGTERM->grace->SIGKILLs the watchdog sweep process; this is best-effort and wrapped so a kill failure never breaks deregister (NON-FATAL).

remote-sandbox-sync.sh two-level layout: base/ seeded once per slug with atomic remote mkdir lock; per-task overlay uses --link-dest for hard-linked unchanged files; all slug trees nested under sandbox/ sub-dir; --sandbox-key <slug>/<subpath> overrides only the overlay suffix (the warm base stays keyed by SLUG alone).
remote-sandbox-sync.sh resolves REMOTE_HOME via ssh printf (tilde expansion unreliable in --link-dest).
remote-sandbox-sync.sh TASK_ID rejects the literal value 'base' and all path-traversal patterns; --sandbox-key must be exactly '<segment>/<segment>' and its subpath may not be 'base' either.

run-status.sh, normalize-task-state.sh, overnight-preflight.sh, and morning-report.py have moved to the overnight-run concept doc (docs/llm/overnight-run.json); the follow-up sink family (sink-*.sh/.py, notion-push.py, followup-reconcile-notion*, parse-followups-block.py, validate-followup-schemas.sh) has moved to the followup-sink concept doc (docs/llm/followup-sink.json). This concept doc no longer covers those files.
gotchas: block-dangerous-git.sh is fail-closed: if git branch -r --contains errors (detached HEAD, no remote, git error), it blocks the rewrite verb rather than allowing it through.

block-dangerous-git.sh normalizes commands before classification: splits on &&/||/|/;/& chain operators and strips git global options (-C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree, etc.) so evasion via git -C /tmp reset --hard or GIT_DIR=x git reset --hard is not possible.

block-dangerous-git.sh +-refspec push (git push origin +main) is treated as a force push and flows through the upstream-reachability check. Plain git push origin main (no +) is not a force push and passes through unconditionally.
block-dangerous-git.sh accepts empty or non-JSON stdin gracefully (fails safe by allowing). Non-Bash tool calls pass through immediately.
Z_HARNESS_GIT_GUARDRAILS_OVERRIDE=1 is a one-shot escape hatch (one invocation); it is not a permanent disable. Each override appends one audit entry.

log-event.sh routes base-path resolution through z_harness_base() (plan-path.sh); when Z_HARNESS_BASE_DIR is set, mid-flight legacy detection is skipped entirely to preserve the model.patch invariant.

log-event.sh Hermes marker emission maps event kind context_pressure to marker kind heartbeat and everything else to status; the marker task field is SLUG (falling back to RUN, then the literal 'orchestration'). Failures are swallowed (>/dev/null 2>&1 || true) so a broken marker path never breaks the primary event write.
log-phase.sh check_wall_ms threshold 604_800_000ms catches seconds-vs-ms overflow (1500x headroom); wall_ms_negative covers NTP jumps / clock skew.
macOS BSD date lacks %3N support; log-phase.sh falls back to python3 time.time()*1000.
log-event.sh silently wraps non-JSON payloads as {"raw": ...} instead of failing.

log-phase.sh begin/finish: shell variables die across Bash tool-call boundaries causing wall_ms:0; begin/finish use $TMPDIR files to persist T0. finish is fail-open: missing stamp = silent no-op, not a bogus wall_ms:0 event.

config.py startup guards check: every QUESTION_IDS key exists in VALIDATORS; every entry has non-null skill_default; every entry has a halt_category in HALT_CATEGORY_ENUM; every RESULT_MAP (question_id, choice) references known question_id and valid choice.
config.py resolve-question: Z_HARNESS_ASK_ALL=1 short-circuits to result=ask regardless of config/memory; Z_HARNESS_EXPLAIN_RESOLUTION=1 enables verbose stderr explain output.
config.py resolve-question: Z_HARNESS_ASK_ALL=1 and Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt set simultaneously exits 5.
config.py resolve-question: workflow.spec_retro_discovery can return defer-to-sink when set to defer_to_sink_p2; callers must handle this result by invoking sink-add.sh instead of prompting.
config.py check-no-ask: unregistered question_id always halts (fail-closed) and emits unknown_ask_blocked event when Z_HARNESS_NO_ASK=halt.
config.py get-batch: always exits 0 (best-effort); callers should fall back to per-key defaults for null values. Meta keys (e.g. roles.*) are excluded silently.
config.py resolve-halt-category: outputs bare string not JSON; fail-safe 'ask' for unknown qids; chain-runner uses this to classify gate categories without needing the full resolver envelope.

config.py model_classes/model_routing are new (2026-07-05, codex prod release) — model_routing.native_agents.default is empty-string by default so native agents keep their checked-in frontmatter model; only agents with an explicit model_routing.native_agents.<agent> override deviate. model_routing.implementer.* reproduces the pre-existing /z-execute implementer tier→model labels (low/medium=sonnet, high/retry=opus) as configurable routes (e.g. gpt-5.5 under omp).

active-plan-registry.py sets OBJC_DISABLE_INITIALIZE_FORK_SAFETY=YES at import time to prevent CoreFoundation fork-safety crashes (macOS only: bash-invoked Python with existing CF-initialized parent).

active-plan-registry.py session-id: Linux uses /proc/<ppid>/stat + /proc/stat for stable <ppid>-<start_epoch>; macOS uses pure-Python <ppid>-<int(time.time())> (no subprocess). Callers should export Z_HARNESS_SESSION_ID once at run start.
active-plan-registry.py heartbeat: absent record emits registry_error(reason:missing_record) and returns 0 (no-op). Does NOT fabricate zombie records — empty slug/session pollutes overlap detection.

active-plan-registry.py overlaps: exit 4 when active_plans_dir cannot be resolved (not a clean 0/10/20 exit). Stale peers (status:stale OR heartbeat > stale_threshold) are non-blocking even in strict mode.

active-plan-registry.py reap: FileNotFoundError on unlink is always benign (two reapers racing on the same record). All OSErrors during reap are suppressed (non-fatal). reap is the one deliberate exception to the single-writer invariant — marking a PEER's record status:stale.

active-plan-registry.py: callers MUST check exit code 3 from register — it is the only LOUD failure among the mutating subcommands. wait-for is the other subcommand with LOUD non-zero exits (2 usage, 10 timeout, 130 signal); all other subcommands are non-fatal by design.

active-plan-registry.py claim/release/wait-for (F1-F5 lease subsystem) are implemented and unit-tested but, as of this refresh, no shipped skill under skills/ invokes claim, release, or wait-for — only session-id/register/heartbeat/update-scope/list/overlaps/reap/deregister are wired into live commands. Treat the lease trio as available-but-not-yet-consumed infrastructure.

active-plan-registry.py wait-for reads runtime.auto_wait (bool) and runtime.auto_wait_budget_secs from config.py to choose auto vs explicit-timeout mode; explicit mode falls back to Z_HARNESS_WAIT_TIMEOUT_SECS / Z_HARNESS_WAIT_POLL_SECS env vars. Z_HARNESS_WAIT_REQUIRE_MERGE is read but reserved (deferred branch-ancestor check) — an age-stale target with status still 'running' already counts as cleared regardless of this flag.

run-memory-review.sh AXIOM_READY: only emitted on the STATUS: ready path, not on skip paths. Axiom extraction checks axioms.auto_extract_post_run via config.py get; unavailable config defaults to 'true' (enabled).

[rotation] persona-stats.py baseline: no-persona is the primary null baseline (true null prefix); boring-anchor is the secondary control. BOTH appear as their own rows in every section — neither is quarantined or hidden from reporting.
[rotation] persona-stats.py --since filter: events with missing or unparseable ts excluded (conservative) — not included with or without the flag.
[rotation] persona-stats.py run=='unknown-run' exclusion: these are ad-hoc test/dev draws with no real run/task/attempt context; excluded by default.
version.sh degrades gracefully if plugin root is not a git repo, returning non-git sentinel values.
extract-dismissals.py drops findings lacking a title field; does NOT fall back to T-MR-NNN ids (renumbered each run).
remote-sandbox-sync.sh warns but does not fail when no .z-harness-rsync-exclude is found.
remote-sandbox-sync.sh seed_base: failed rsync cleans up partial base dir before releasing lock.
remote-sandbox-sync.sh all slug trees now nested under sandbox/ sub-dir of the container root; a misdirected rsync can no longer pollute alongside real slug dirs.

remote-sandbox-sync.sh Z_HARNESS_WORKTREE_ROOT: when the orchestrator's cwd is the main checkout but edits land in a linked worktree, the default git rev-parse --show-toplevel resolves the main tree and ships stale files; set Z_HARNESS_WORKTREE_ROOT to the worktree's absolute path to override (hard-errors, exit 2, if the path does not exist). The resolved source root is always printed to stderr as 'syncing local root: <path>'.

lint-askuser.sh and preflight.sh remain in the scripts/ directory but are no longer covered by any concept doc's declared source_file list after this refresh (they dropped out of this doc's scope and are not present in followup-sink.json or overnight-run.json either) — flagged for the caller to assign a concept home.
